title: Reconciler: one epic at concurrency one — claims, waves, gates, merge, boundary, cleanup ordering, restart from a clone
description:
internal/reconcile and ticfac run-epic <id>: read the epic graph through the tk client; claim the next dispatchable tick; start a job through the executor; inspect on a bounded cadence (well under any wipe threshold); collect; boundary-check; merge the attempt branch into the EpicRun integration branch epic/<id>; run the integrated gate from [testing.commands] in .tick/runners.toml (nothing else authorizes shell); close durably through tk only after the gate; clean up only after the close; write a checkpoint on every state change and an attempt record per dispatch through internal/runstate; every effect preceded by the CAS that proves it has not happened. Restart: ticfac run-epic on a fresh clone reads .ticfac/ and adopts live attempts by identity, never redispatches a live one, settles in-flight states from durable evidence, and continues. Appendix A invariants #1-#13 hold; run the lifecycle-invariants suite against the REAL reconciler+executor via an adapter, not only the fake harness. EPIC-SKELETON respected: review and closeout ticks are dispatched last, as jobs (profiles in the next tick). No event bus, no plugin system, no multi-epic.

## How this fits
Wave 3 of epic qeu. Integration commit d609c8e73548e7530d980d1e9b716e051cc4722d on epic/qeu contains everything you build on — read each package's doc.go and the RESULT reports recorded in the commit messages/notes: internal/exec/subprocess (qg5: New(Options{Repo, StateDir, Runner, Remote, Attempt, PushInterval}), Start/Inspect/Cancel/Collect/CollectDetail/Dispose/RequestStop, typed Refusals via AsRefusal; Start ADOPTS a live attempt and HOLDS an unanswerable one — never treat RefusedUnknown as dead; the five invariants it does not cover — A3 step cap, A4 poll/keepalive, A11 strike-out, A12 budget clamping, A13 evidence fingerprinting — are listed in its lifecycle_test.go uncoveredInvariants and are YOURS), internal/runstate (xkd: Open(Options{Repo, Remote, Branch, RunID}) then Fetch, PutCheckpoint/PutAttempt/PutDecision/PutEvidence returning (Outcome, error) — check Outcome.EffectPermitted() before every effect; readers Checkpoint/Attempt(s)/Decision(s)/Evidence; never point a Store at a checkout with the integration branch checked out if you call CommitLocal), internal/tk (y7o: contract-1 client for the 15 manifest commands; real tk on PATH serves contract 1), internal/contracts + internal/schema, and the parity lifecycle harness (internal/contracts/parity/lifecycle_harness_test.go) whose 13 invariants you must run against the REAL reconciler+executor through an adapter. You own internal/reconcile and cmd/ticfac (run-epic wiring) — a sibling tick (vcx) is editing internal/exec/subprocess concurrently, so do not modify that package; if the executor needs a change, report it in RESULT-px2.md as a concern instead. No third-party deps (stdlib only), do not touch go.mod, README.md or contracts/. The only shell you may run from the reconciler is [testing.commands] in the target repo's .tick/runners.toml (write a minimal TOML reader for that table or reuse one if it exists — check internal/ first). Verify your base: git merge-base --is-ancestor d609c8e73548e7530d980d1e9b716e051cc4722d HEAD.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture epic (3 ticks, 2 waves, review, closeout) completes end to end with a fake runner; restart after dispatch, after collection and before closure produces no duplicate attempt and no false close (three table tests that kill the reconciler at each point and rerun it from a fresh clone); the lifecycle-invariants suite is green against the real components; go test -short ./... green.
